duration.$description: Motion durations — fast and functional (150–250ms), never choreography.

fast.$description: Generic short transition — alias of the state duration.

normal.$description: Standard enter/exit for surfaces and overlays

reduced.$description: Reduced-motion alternative — effectively instant, but deliberately 1ms rather than 0ms. A zero-duration transition or animation never fires transitionend or animationend, so any cleanup, focus hand-off, or promise that awaits those events hangs forever under prefers-reduced-motion. 1ms is imperceptible and still dispatches the event.

easing.$description: Easing curves. standard and linear are the functional defaults; the named curves below are for directional motion and are referenced by component tokens rather than used ad hoc. standard carries the Material 3 curve, and balanced is a compatibility alias of it.

standard.$description: Default functional easing — the Material 3 standard curve, balanced enter/exit. Deliberately not the CSS `ease` keyword: `ease` is the browser default that applies when no easing is authored, so emitting it as the kernel's standard curve makes designed and undesigned motion indistinguishable, and a consumer that overrides `easing.standard` with a real curve silently loses it when this layer loads last.

balanced.$description: Compatibility alias of easing.standard, retained so existing references keep resolving. Prefer easing.standard.

accelerate.$description: Content exiting — starts slow, exits quickly

decelerate.$description: Content entering — starts fast, settles gently
